name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)
briefDescription: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) runs Janaushadhi Kendras — affordable generic medicine outlets — across India. The scheme also allows pharmacists, entrepreneurs and NGOs to open a Kendra and earn a 20% incentive on monthly PMBI purchases, up to ₹20,000/month.
descriptionMd:
Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), run by the Department of Pharmaceuticals (Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers) through PMBI (Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India), aims to make quality generic medicines available to all citizens at affordable prices. It does this by setting up dedicated outlets called **Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs)** where branded-equivalent generic medicines are sold at a fraction of the market price.

The scheme has a dual benefit: citizens get cheaper medicines, and pharmacy professionals or entrepreneurs running a Kendra earn a sustainable livelihood through incentives from PMBI.
benefitsMd:
**For citizens (buyers):**
- Quality generic medicines available at PMBJKs at prices **50%–90% lower** than branded medicines.
- Over 1,900 medicines and 300 surgical/nutraceutical products available under the scheme.

**For Kendra operators (entrepreneurs/pharmacists):**
- A **20% incentive on monthly net purchases** from PMBI, subject to a ceiling of **₹20,000 per month** (₹2.40 lakh/year).
- Incentive is disbursed in two parts — 50% upfront on purchase and 50% on meeting targets.
- Special monthly incentive of **₹15,000** for Kendras in special areas (Himalayan regions, islands, tribal and backward areas, NE states).
- **One-time setup support** of ₹2 lakh (₹1.5 lakh for furniture/computers + ₹0.5 lakh for medicines) in special-category areas.
eligibilityMd:
Anyone who meets the licensing requirements for a pharmacy can open a Janaushadhi Kendra:

**Individual pharmacists or entrepreneurs:**
- Must hold a **D.Pharma or B.Pharma degree**, or employ a qualified pharmacist on the premises.

**NGOs, SHGs, Trusts and Charitable Organisations:**
- Must employ a B.Pharma/D.Pharma degree holder to manage the Kendra.

**Government hospital/medical college premises:**
- Preference to reputed NGOs/charitable organisations, though individuals also qualify.
- Must employ qualified pharmacist staff.

Premises of at least **10 sq m** are required, and the applicant must not run any other pharmaceutical business from the same premises.
applicationMd:
**Step 1:** Visit the official PMBI portal at [janaushadhi.gov.in](https://janaushadhi.gov.in/).
**Step 2:** Navigate to the **'Apply Online'** section for Janaushadhi Kendra registration.
**Step 3:** Fill in your personal details, pharmacy qualification details, and proposed Kendra location.
**Step 4:** Upload the required documents: ID proof, pharmacy degree certificate (or employee's degree), premises proof, NOC from local authority, and drug licence (or application).
**Step 5:** Submit the application and pay the application fee (if applicable) online.

After PMBI reviews your application, they may conduct a site visit before issuing approval and onboarding you to the PoS software for ordering medicines.
